title: $100M Offers
author: Alex Hormozi
blurb: Alex Hormozi argues that most businesses struggle not because of weak marketing, but because their offer is ordinary. When you sell the same thing as everyone else, buyers compare on price, and everyone races to the bottom. His answer is the Grand Slam Offer, a package so valuable that turning it down feels foolish. First, he shows how to choose a starving crowd: people with urgent pain, money to spend, and easy access. He explains why charging more can make you better at serving customers. At the heart of the book is a value equation. You raise the dream outcome and the buyer's belief it will happen, while cutting the waiting time and the effort required. Then you list every obstacle your customer faces, turn each one into a solution, and bundle them together. Scarcity, urgency, bonuses, guarantees and smart naming make the offer even stronger.

lessons.b: When your offer looks like everyone else's, buyers compare on price, so you need a unique Grand Slam Offer that cannot be compared.
The market you choose matters more than your offer or your persuasion skills, so pick people with urgent pain, money to spend, easy access, and a growing need.
Premium prices create a virtuous cycle, because more margin lets you deliver better results and attract more committed customers.
Value rises with the dream outcome and the buyer's belief they will get it, and it falls with the time it takes and the effort it costs.
issues: scene 7: The shoulder arc under the head runs off the bottom edge, and its right side passes through the 'visualgrowth.app' footer brand text. (fix: Shift the head-and-shoulders figure up and left, or shorten the shoulder arc so it ends above y≈820 and clear of the footer brand area.)

scene 8: The 'Time' and 'Effort' labels in the shrunken denominator boxes are about 18px or smaller at 1600 width, which is barely legible. (fix: Keep the boxes visibly small to show 'shrinking', but raise the label text to at least 22px (widen the boxes slightly if needed), or put the labels just below the boxes at a readable size.)

lessons.t: Turn Problems Into a Stacked Offer
lessons.b: List every obstacle your customer faces, turn each into a solution, choose how to deliver it, then trim and stack the best pieces into one package.
issues: scene 6: The 'PRIVATE SESSIONS' label in the CUT zone is pale grey text with a strikethrough, sitting on a light indigo fill. Contrast is very low and the label is hard to read, yet it is the key example in the narration. (fix: Render the label in ink navy or indigo at full opacity on a white pill. Keep the strikethrough at a thinner weight, or show the 'cut' with a separate indigo line or X mark, so the words stay legible.)

lessons.b: Scarcity, urgency, bonuses, guarantees and a compelling name make a strong offer even harder to refuse.

lessons.t: Making People Feel Stupid Saying No
lessons.b: The right crowd, a confident price, the value equation and smart enhancers combine into an offer that sells itself.
